title: Let a host report a measured, unchanged named root as a sighting without opening change obligations
outcome: Let a host report a measured, unchanged named root as a sighting without opening change obligations
acceptance: The host protocol's execution_observe source_change accepts a new additive detection for a measured, unchanged workspace. It carries the workspace, the host's retained earlier measurement, and the current measured sighting, with equal revisions. Every existing detection keeps its current meaning, validation and refusals, including content_comparison's refusal of an equal pair.

A record with the new detection, accounted under the current policy for the run's newest claim epoch, whose sighting matches the root basis (workspace, generation, named state), counts as a named-root sighting for acceptance-evaluation admission and consumption at its run-feed position.

The new detection is never read as a source change. It opens no obligations, discharges no existing obligation, clears no freshness, asserts nothing about edits between the two measurements, grants no admission, and credits no test or check.

A record whose sighting does not match the root basis is refused as other sightings are. An audit-only policy basis, a historical binding, a finished run or a moved root basis is accounted audit-only and is not a sighting.

Tests cover: the accepted sighting enabling an evaluation that was refused for no sighting; no obligation opened; the audit-only cases; validation refusing unequal revisions, mismatched workspaces, and a baseline observed after its sighting; and replay of the same idempotency key.
The host protocol documentation and docs/shipped.md describe the new detection and the cases a host should use it in, consistent with the existing detections.

When Engram already holds a measured sighting in that workspace at a revision other than the one reported as unchanged, the new detection is refused with a typed refusal that tells the host to report a content comparison from Engram's newest revision, and nothing is recorded; a test covers it. When Engram holds no measured sighting in the workspace, the host's own retained baseline stands.
The new detection is refused on the admitted turn-checkpoint path, which this item does not design; a test covers it.
